name: Apliki copper district
observation: Lead-isotope work links the copper in analyzed Late Bronze Age oxhide ingots, including the Uluburun assemblage, to Cypriot ore and especially the Apliki mining region.
limits: Ore compatibility is not a voyage log, and later research may refine which Cypriot mine or production stage supplied individual ingots.

name: Uluburun shipwreck
observation: The wreck carried approximately ten tonnes of copper and one tonne of tin as separate raw-metal cargoes.
limits: One exceptional wreck is not an annual trade total, a complete cargo manifest for the whole economy, or proof that every shipment used a ten-to-one ratio.

name: Cornwall and Devon tin province
observation: Chemical and isotopic similarities make south-west Britain a plausible source for part of the Uluburun tin cargo.
limits: The 2023 reassessment calls this possible rather than incontrovertible; it does not establish a direct Britain-to-Uluburun route.

name: Mušiston
observation: A 2022 study proposed Mušiston as a source for part of the cargo; a 2023 reanalysis argues that this specific polymetallic deposit cannot match the Uluburun tin.
limits: Rejecting Mušiston does not rule out every eastern tin source or solve the provenance of the complete cargo.

name: Taurus and Bolkardağ region
observation: Lead in many ingots resembles ores in the Taurus region, but the lead may have entered during pooling or processing rather than identifying the tin ore itself.
limits: Lead association is not a secure tin-source match; Anatolian tin remains a less likely but not wholly excluded interpretation.

name: Apliki copper district
observation: Nearly 200 ore analyses provided a Cypriot baseline; 78 analyzed oxhide ingots were isotopically consistent with northern Cypriot ore, especially Apliki.
limits: The sample does not include every oxhide ingot, and analytical compatibility should not be drawn as a single known shipping route.

name: Cyprus
observation: Analyzed oxhide ingots from Cyprus fall within the northern Cypriot ore signature.
limits: This is a find-region summary within the published 78-ingot sample, not a count for Cyprus or a complete distribution inventory.

name: Crete
observation: Analyzed oxhide ingots found on Crete fall within the northern Cypriot ore signature.
limits: The connection is geochemical provenance, not a reconstructed direct sailing leg from Apliki to Crete.

name: Greece
observation: Analyzed oxhide ingots found in Greece fall within the northern Cypriot ore signature.
limits: The connection is geochemical provenance, not a reconstructed direct sailing leg or a total of Greek copper imports.

name: Sardinia
observation: Analyzed oxhide ingots found on Sardinia fall within the northern Cypriot ore signature.
limits: The connection is geochemical provenance, not a reconstructed direct sailing leg or proof of one centralized distribution system.

name: Anatolian coast
observation: Analyzed oxhide ingots found in Turkey fall within the northern Cypriot ore signature.
limits: The marker summarizes a country-scale find region and does not locate every find or identify one port of entry.

name: Bulgaria
observation: Analyzed oxhide ingots found in Bulgaria fall within the northern Cypriot ore signature.
limits: The marker summarizes a country-scale find region and does not reconstruct the path by which the metal reached the Balkans.

name: Cornwall and Devon tin province
observation: Trace elements plus lead and tin isotopes link several Bronze Age Mediterranean shipwreck ingots to south-west British ores.
limits: Analytical provenance does not identify the traders, intermediate exchanges, ports, or exact path taken by any ingot.

name: Salcombe and Erme finds
observation: Tin ingots recovered off south-west Britain provide an archaeological and analytical comparator for the British source signal.
limits: The offshore finds are not a mine assemblage or a complete record of tin leaving Britain.

name: Israeli coast shipwrecks
observation: Tin ingots from three shipwrecks off Israel are fully consistent with ores from Cornwall and Devon in the 2025 study.
limits: The study explicitly finds no evidence for a direct Britain-to-eastern-Mediterranean connection; down-the-line movement is inferred.

name: Sardinia
observation: Sardinia had eastern and western metal connections and is proposed as one possible intermediary in a down-the-line tin network.
limits: Possible intermediary status is a network hypothesis, not proof that the analyzed Israeli ingots passed through Sardinia.

name: Mari archive
observation: A text preserved at Mari records tin trade at Ugarit involving Minoans and a translator.
limits: The tablet records a transaction and linguistic mediation; it does not reveal the mine source, cargo size, or complete route.

name: Ugarit
observation: Ugarit appears as a coastal hub where tin trade with Minoans was conducted.
limits: The text does not establish that every later metal cargo used Ugarit or that palace actors monopolized the exchange.

name: Minoan Aegean
observation: Minoan traders appear in the Mari text's account of tin exchange at Ugarit, with a translator assisting.
limits: The broad marker does not identify a specific Minoan polity, vessel, or sailing route.
